reading.body:
This incident is recorded as a failure of the reporting record rather than a documented failure of a deployed system. The summary states that the underlying article text could not be read as news content, so the incident as catalogued contains no established account of what an AI system did, who operated it, or what harm followed. The only concrete facts are the titles and dates of the three reports and the fact that two outlets are counted.

What is shown is a mismatch between an incident entry and its evidence. The entry carries a title about AI pricing at McDonald's, while the reports listed include a judge's warning about AI and lawyer training and a declaration, and the summary describes raw PDF structure rather than readable reporting. Nothing in the given facts establishes that an AI pricing system was deployed, tested, or caused any outcome, and nothing establishes that the judge's warning concerned the same subject as the McDonald's headline.

It is not established whether these reports describe one event or several, whether any allegation in them was tested, or whether the unreadable document is the declaration named in the report list. A title is not a finding, and an unreadable file is not evidence of what a system did.
